**Proof.**

Let $G$ be a finite connected simplicial complex, so $G$ is a compact Hausdorff space (it is the geometric realization of a finite simplicial complex, hence a finite union of compact simplices). Let $p \colon \widetilde{G} \to G$ be the universal covering map. Since $G$ is a connected, locally path-connected, and semilocally simply connected space (any simplicial complex has these properties), the universal cover exists and the group of deck transformations is isomorphic to $\pi_1(G)$.

For any basepoint $x_0 \in G$, the fiber $p^{-1}(x_0)$ is in bijection with the set of right cosets of the trivial subgroup $\{e\} \leq \pi_1(G, x_0)$, i.e. with $\pi_1(G, x_0)$ itself. Concretely, lifting classes of loops gives a canonical bijection
$$\pi_1(G, x_0) \;\longrightarrow\; p^{-1}(x_0), \qquad [\gamma] \mapsto \widetilde{\gamma}(1),$$
where $\widetilde{\gamma}$ is the lift of $\gamma$ starting at a chosen basepoint $\widetilde{x}_0 \in p^{-1}(x_0)$. Hence the number of sheets of the covering equals $\lvert \pi_1(G)\rvert$, which is finite by hypothesis.

So $p \colon \widetilde{G} \to G$ is a finite-sheeted covering map. A finite-sheeted covering of a compact space is compact: if $\{U_\alpha\}$ is an open cover of $\widetilde{G}$, then for each $x \in G$ choose an evenly covered neighborhood $V_x$; the finitely many sheets over $V_x$ are each covered by finitely many $U_\alpha$ (using compactness of the closure, or more directly, since there are finitely many sheets and each sheet over $V_x$ is homeomorphic to $V_x$). Compactness of $G$ gives finitely many $V_{x_i}$ covering $G$, and the finitely many sheets over these finitely many $V_{x_i}$ are covered by finitely many $U_\alpha$. Thus $\widetilde{G}$ is compact.

Therefore, finiteness of $\pi_1(G)$ implies that the universal cover of $G$ is compact. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
